name: inbox
description: List-detail split view (messages, tickets, conversations) driven entirely by declarative directives: one l-data holds the selected id, ':hidden' bindings swap the detail pane, ':data-state' marks which pane is active, and the list is l-for-shaped so it can be bound to an l-source collection without changing the markup. Below the small breakpoint it collapses to the active pane with back navigation. Zero custom JavaScript — it needs faqir-core.js, nothing else.

list-pane.description: The message column. Label it with aria-labelledby pointing at the list heading, and bind :data-state to active/inactive — below 640px the inactive pane is hidden

list-header.description: Row above the list holding the heading and a count badge or filter control

list-heading.description: Name of the mailbox or queue. Give it an id and point the list pane's aria-labelledby at it

search.description: Optional search field over the list. A bare input primitive with its own aria-label — the pattern does no filtering itself

status.description: Loading line for a server-bound list — bind :hidden to the source's <name>Loading flag and give it role='status'

error.description: Error line for a server-bound list — bind :hidden and l-text to the source's <name>Error string and give it role='alert'

list.description: The message list. A real <ul>; each <li> holds one item button, authored or produced by an l-for template

item.description: One message row, and a real <button>: selecting is @click='selected = <id>'. The open row carries data-state='selected' AND aria-current='true' so the selection is not colour-only

item-sender.description: Who the message is from, in the row

item-time.description: When it arrived, already formatted for display (the pattern never formats dates)

item-subject.description: Subject line of the row, truncated to one line

item-preview.description: First lines of the body, clamped to two lines

detail-pane.description: The reading column: the back button, one detail per message, and the empty state. Bind :data-state to active/inactive like the list pane. Not a landmark — each detail names itself

back.description: Clears the selection ('@click=selected = null'), which makes the list pane active again. Hidden by CSS above 640px, where both panes are visible and there is nothing to go back to

detail.description: One message, shown only when it is the selected one (':hidden=selected !== <id>'). Authored details also carry a static hidden attribute as the pre-boot guard

detail-subject.description: Subject of the open message. Give it an id and point the detail's aria-labelledby at it

detail-meta.description: Sender, address and timestamp of the open message. It WRAPS the horizontal stack that lines the avatar up with the text — put the part on the wrapper, because a data-part inside the stack would belong to the stack

detail-body.description: The message body. Omit it when the body lives in a nested tabs panel instead — a data-part inside tabs would belong to tabs, not to the inbox

detail-actions.description: Reply/archive row, pinned to the bottom of the detail

empty.description: Shown when nothing is selected (':hidden=selected !== null'). Wraps the empty-state pattern; it is the wrapper, not the empty-state itself, that carries the part

active.description: This pane is the one worth showing: the list while nothing is selected, the reading pane once something is. Above 640px it changes nothing — both panes are visible

inactive.description: The other pane. Below the canon md floor (768px), where there is room for one, the inactive pane is display:none — that IS the responsive collapse

selected.description: The open message's row. Pair it with aria-current='true' so the selection is not signalled by colour alone

required_attrs: aria-labelledby on the list pane pointing at the list heading id
each message row is a real button, so it is one tab stop with Enter/Space activation
aria-current='true' on the selected row, alongside data-state='selected'
aria-labelledby on each authored detail pointing at its own subject id
role='status' on the loading line and role='alert' on the error line of a server-bound list
an aria-label on the search input — the pattern ships no visible label for it

keyboard.Tab: move through the search field, the message rows, and the actions of the open message
keyboard.Enter / Space on the back button: clear the selection and, in the collapsed layout, return to the list

templates.html:
{mailbox}

{unread}

{subject}

{initials} {meta}
{body}

{empty_title}

{empty_description}
templates.html_source:
{mailbox}

0 messages

Loading messages…

{empty_title}

{empty_description}

data_shape.note: What an agent binds where. The pattern owns exactly one piece of state — `selected` — and reads a collection of messages. Both templates render the same markup; `html_source` is `html` with the authored rows replaced by l-for templates over an l-source collection.

scope.selected: string | null — the id of the open message. null renders the empty state and makes the list pane the active one. It is the ONLY state the pattern owns; everything else is derived by bindings

message.target: one [data-part='item'] in the list and one [data-part='detail'] in the pane, both keyed by the same id

item.id: string — the value written into `selected`; must be unique within the inbox
item.sender: string — [data-part='item-sender'] and the detail meta line
item.time: string — already formatted for display; the pattern never formats dates
item.subject: string — [data-part='item-subject'] and [data-part='detail-subject']
item.preview: string — [data-part='item-preview'], clamped to two lines by CSS
item.body: string — [data-part='detail-body'] via l-text. Bind rich bodies server-side instead: the pattern never sets innerHTML

source.directive: l-source:messages="/api/messages" on the root, beside l-data
source.injects: `messages` (the array), `messagesLoading` (boolean) and `messagesError` (string | null) into the same scope the bindings read, plus the `$messages` controller for load/create/update/remove
source.binds: [data-part='status'] to :hidden="!messagesLoading", [data-part='error'] to :hidden="!messagesError" + l-text="messagesError", and both l-for templates to `messages`
source.note: Selection survives a refresh only if the ids do: key the l-for with l-key="message.id" so rows follow their message, and the open detail stays open

notes: Slot ownership: a data-part belongs to its nearest data-ui ancestor. Inside the nested tabs the parts (list, trigger, panel) are TABS' parts, and inside [data-part='empty'] they are the empty-state's — which is why the empty wrapper carries the part rather than the empty-state itself, and why a detail whose body lives in a tabs panel simply omits [data-part='detail-body'].

A nested primitive must not carry both data-part and data-variant: a part's data-variant is validated against the INBOX's variant values. That is why the back button is a data-ui='button' with no data-variant, and why the horizontal stack sits INSIDE [data-part='detail-meta'] rather than being it.

Every authored element a binding hides also ships the static `hidden` attribute as a pre-boot guard: without it the whole thread would flash before faqir-core boots. The elements that are visible in the authored state (the first detail, the empty state of a source-bound inbox) must NOT carry it.

The responsive collapse is pure CSS keyed on each pane's data-state, which a :data-state binding derives from `selected`. There is no matchMedia, no resize listener and no JavaScript of any kind in this pattern.

The state lives on the PANES rather than on the [data-ui="inbox"] root for a concrete reason: faqir-core does not yet apply bind directives declared on an l-data scope root (FAQIR-PLAN follow-up 0.6-15), so a :data-state on the root would render once and then never update. Anything reactive must sit below the element that carries l-data.

changes.note: The pane collapse moves onto the breakpoint canon, mobile-first (task 0.8-09). The single-pane layout is now the unconditional base and @media (min-width: 48rem) adds the second pane, which moves the collapse floor from an ad-hoc 640px to the canon md tier (768px). MIGRATION: viewports from 640px to 767px — a small tablet in portrait — now get the single-pane layout with [data-part='back'] visible, where 1.x gave them two panes; there is no tier between sm and md to land on, and 22rem of list plus a message body does not fit in 700px. The list column still widens to 22rem at lg. The pattern also gains an intrinsic height below md (block-size: auto with a 24rem floor) instead of a fixed 32rem box, so a phone scrolls the page rather than the pane.
